sections.label: Bill amendments effective date
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments take effect on 10 May 2022, one day after the Bill's First Reading.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: If passed by Parliament, the amendments in the Bill will take effect on 10 May 2022, that is, one day after the First Reading of the Bill.

sections.label: ABSD for trusts introduction
sections.summary: After studying how transfers of residential properties into trusts would be treated, ABSD (Trust) was introduced on 8 May 2022, effective 9 May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As trusts are complex instruments and serve diverse purposes, the Government carefully studied the issue before deciding on how transfers of residential properties into trusts would be treated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We then introduced Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty for Trust, or ABSD (Trust), on 8 May 2022, which took effect on 9 May 2022.

sections.label: ACD (Trust) rates
sections.summary: If ACD (Trust) applies, the trustee pays prevailing ACD rates of up to 44%, comprising 40% ABSD and up to 4% BSD.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: If ACD (Trust) applies, the trustee will be liable to pay ACD (Trust) at the prevailing ACD rates of up to 44% for buyers, comprising 40% ABSD and up to 4% BSD.

sections.label: Fine for failure to notify
sections.summary: The original beneficial owner is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $1,000 for failure to give notice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For his or her failure to give notice, the original beneficial owner will be liable, on conviction, to a fine not exceeding $1,000.

sections.label: SSD and late payment penalties
sections.summary: Renouncing the interest within three years makes the original beneficial owner liable for SSD, and late or unpaid duty carries a penalty of up to four times the duty payable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: If the interest in the trust residential property is renounced within three years after the original beneficial owner first has beneficial ownership of the interest, the original beneficial owner will also be liable to pay SSD.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For any duty paid late or not paid, the original beneficial owner or the settlor will have to pay a penalty of up to four times the duty payable, which is the penalty under the current Stamp Duties Act.

sections.label: Harmonising stamp duty for trusts
sections.summary: The motion harmonises stamp duty treatment for equity interests held in trust, and ACD (Trust) with ABSD (Trust) will raise tax revenues and help stabilise the property market.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On that, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will harmonise the stamp duty treatment for equity interests held in trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: ACD (Trust), along with the introduction of Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) for transfer of residential property into a living trust – ABSD (Trust) – will help to raise tax revenues and go towards stabilising the property market.

sections.label: ABSD Trust start date
sections.summary: The new ABSD (Trust) applies only to instruments executed on or after 9 May 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new ABSD (Trust) will only apply to instruments executed on or after 9 May 2022.

sections.label: Stamp duty receipts higher
sections.summary: FY2021 stamp duty receipts rose from a $4.25 billion Budget 2021 estimate to $6.76 billion actual, about $2.5 billion or 59% higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More recently, stamp duty receipts in FY2021 have turned out to be higher than what was initially projected by the Government, from an initial estimate of $4.25 billion in Budget 2021 to the revised estimate of $6.45 billion as of Budget 2022, to actual receipts of $6.76 billion, which, I believe, is a record high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, the positive surprise to stamp duty receipts worked out to be about $2.5 billion or 59% higher, as compared to what was initially budgeted for in Budget 2021.

sections.label: FY2021 operating revenues
sections.summary: FY2021 operating revenues were $82.5 billion, $5.8 billion above the Budget 2021 figure and $2.1 billion above the revised estimate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Overall, operating revenues worked out to be $82.5 billion for FY2021, $5.8 billion higher, compared to $76.6 billion as initially budgeted for in Budget 2021 and $2.1 billion higher than the revised estimate of $80.4 billion as of Budget 2022.

sections.label: ABSD ACD signalling effect
sections.summary: The question asks whether the ABSD and ACD (Trusts) were meant to signal the market amid firm prices and a $85 million Canninghill Piers purchase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With concerns that residential property prices have continued to be firm despite the December cooling measures and amid rising interest rate concerns, was the implementation of the ABSD and ACD (Trusts) meant to achieve a signalling effect to the market, particularly amid news just last month of how an individual acquired 20 units at Canninghill Piers, a luxury condominium along the Singapore River, for over S$85 million, despite the recently raised ABSD rates for foreigners in December last year?

sections.label: HDB stamp duties and trusts
sections.summary: Using a $510,000 Sengkang 4-room resale price, stamp duties would be $9,900, and the Government is asked for trust transfer numbers and values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Using the median resale price of a 4-room HDB flat in Sengkang of $510,000, stamp duties would amount to $9,900.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Again, as part of a periodic policy review, would the Government consider such a move in reducing upfront property purchase costs, particularly with continuing momentum in increasing HDB resale prices, which are now up by a worrying 19% in the last 18 months alone?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are disappointed that the Government has allowed loopholes in the ABSD scheme to be left open and exploited by some rich buyers of properties for so long.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We ask the Government to tell us the number and value of properties transferred to living trusts since the introduction of ABSD in 2011.

sections.label: ABSD on living trusts
sections.summary: The speaker favours applying 35% ABSD on any transfer of residential property into a living trust, even without an identifiable beneficial owner.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.30 pm until 3.50 pm. ﻿Sitting resumed at 3.50 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am in favour of applying the Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) of 35% on any transfer of residential property into a living trust, even if there is no identifiable beneficial owner at the point of transfer.

sections.label: Stamp duty revenue contribution
sections.summary: A Member asks how much more stamp duties are expected to contribute to tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Deputy Speaker, how much more are these stamp duties expected to contribute to our tax revenues?

sections.label: ABSD (Trust) non-application
sections.summary: ABSD (Trust) does not apply because the residential property transfer took place before 9 May 2022, including later trustee distributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Since the transfer of residential property took place before 9 May 2022, ABSD (Trust) does not apply, including to a subsequent distribution of the property by the trustee to a beneficiary of the trust on or after 9 May 2022.

sections.label: No retrospective application of changes
sections.summary: Applying these changes retrospectively to previous transfers would undermine the rule of law and public and business confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai mentioned that we should – if I heard him correctly – retrospectively apply some of these changes to previous transfers, previous transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think it would not be fair or appropriate for us to do that – to apply these changes retrospectively – because this will undermine the rule of law and it would also affect the confidence that the public and businesses have in the certainty that Singapore offers.

sections.label: Fair and progressive tax system
sections.summary: The tax and transfer system is fair and progressive, and the Government has been raising asset-related taxes repeatedly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Overall, our tax and transfer system is fair and progressive and, in fact, the Government has been raising asset-related taxes repeatedly.

sections.label: Trust measures as cooling measures
sections.summary: ABSD (Trust), ACD (Trust) and stamp duty on trust property renunciation are cooling measures, not wealth taxes, with revenue undetermined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: ABSD (Trust), ACD (Trust) and the imposition of stamp duty on the renunciation of a trust property, are not intended to be wealth taxes or revenue-raising measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Rather, they are part of our residential property market cooling measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are unable to determine at this juncture the revenue that will be raised from ABSD (Trust), ACD (Trust) and the stamp duty on the renunciation of a trust property as this depends on the extent to which individuals will transfer a property or equity interests in PHEs into living trusts in future.

sections.label: First-timer families CPF loan servicing
sections.summary: Close to 90% of first-timer families who bought flats this year service housing loans fully using CPF, with no cash payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Close to 90% of first-timer families who bought their flats this year service their housing loans fully using CPF, with no cash payments.

sections.label: ABSD and ACD collection through trusts
sections.summary: Parliament approval of the Bill with amendments would let ABSD and ACD be tracked and imposed whether paid directly or through trusts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If Parliament approves this Bill, with the amendments, moving forward, this is something that, therefore, we will be able to track, we will be able to impose, to ensure that ABSD and ACD are collected, whether it is done directly or through trusts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, we will focus on the contents of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But maybe, just to reiterate, to assure Mr Leong Mun Wai and also Members of the House, that if you look at our tax and benefits system as a whole, and rather than pick and choose individual items, if you consider the tax and benefits system as a whole, where taxes are paid, benefits are given, reallocations are done, Singapore's system is one which is fair and progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Because everybody contributes, but those who earn more, those who have more, will contribute more.
